name: Jungholz
kurzbeschreibung: Tiny exclave – reachable only via Germany – with untouched nature and peaceful tranquility.
beschreibung:
Overview

Jungholz is situated at an elevation of 1,054 metres in the Allgäu Alps within the district of Reutte, Tyrol, representing a fascinating geographical anomaly in Europe. Home to approximately 300 residents, this peaceful mountain village is a functional enclave (pene-enclave): It connects to the rest of Austrian territory at just a single mathematical quadripoint atop the peak of the Sorgschrofen (1,636 m). By road, Jungholz is accessible exclusively across German territory via Wertach or Unterjoch in Upper Bavaria. Positioned far from noisy thoroughfares, Jungholz has earned international recognition as Tyrol's first certified Alpine Herb Village and a cherished, family-friendly sanctuary in both summer and winter, blessed with lush meadows and invigorating alpine air.

History

This territorial curiosity began on June 24, 1342, when Hermann von Schellenberg sold the property ze Junckholtz to Heinz Asch of neighbouring Wertach. In 1343, Tyrolean Regent Duke John Henry ratified the purchase, incorporating Jungholz into the County of Tyrol and the Habsburg realm despite lying geographically behind the mountain crest. Because towering ridges prevented road access from Tyrol, the Austrian Empire and the Kingdom of Bavaria signed the historic Customs Union Treaty on May 3, 1868: Jungholz became part of the German customs area, used the Deutsche Mark until 2002, and still holds two postal codes (Austrian A-6691 and German D-87538). The spiritual focal point is the Baroque Parish Church of the Holy Name of Mary (known as the Herb Church), built in 1714 and dedicated in 1789, decorated with frescoes by Bavarian master Franz Anton Weiß.

Getting There

Access to Jungholz is possible only via Bavaria, Germany. Motorists arriving from Germany can travel completely toll-free and vignette-free via the A7 motorway past Kempten to the Oy-Mittelberg exit, continuing along the B310 to Wertach; from Wertach, it is merely five kilometres into Jungholz. Drivers travelling from Tyrol proceed via Reutte through the Tannheim Valley on the B199 over the Oberjoch pass into Bavaria, heading through Wertach to cross back into Jungholz. Train travellers use Bavarian railway stations at Oy-Mittelberg, Sonthofen, or Kempten, connecting via regional buses directly to the village.

Tips

As Tyrol's 1st Herb Village, Jungholz delights visitors with show gardens surrounding the church and community hall featuring over 100 medicinal plants, accompanied by guided herbal walks and the traditional Herb Festival on August 15. In winter, the Jungholz ski area offers ten family-friendly slope kilometres, child-safe quad chairlifts, and the playful N'Ice Bear Kinderland learning zone. In summer, cool off at the solar-heated Felsenbad outdoor pool nestled against towering natural cliffs. Experienced, sure-footed hikers can embark on the rugged alpine ridge scramble to Mount Sorgschrofen (1,636 m) to see historic Boundary Stone 110 marking the lone point connecting Jungholz to the rest of Tyrol.
